What Is the Accounting Cycle?
The accounting cycle is the standard sequence of steps a business follows to record transactions, summarize them, and produce financial statements — then reset for the next period.

slides.visual_text: A circular diagram called The Cycle with eight numbered steps: 1 Analyze transactions, 2 Journalize entries, 3 Post to ledger, 4 Trial balance, 5 Adjusting entries, 6 Adjusted trial balance, 7 Financial statements, 8 Close accounts. Three notes: Starts with a transaction (a source document such as an invoice or receipt triggers the process); Ends with closed books (temporary accounts reset to zero for the next period); Repeats every period (monthly, quarterly or annually, the cycle never stops).

Personal Accounts
Accounts for people, firms, banks, and other organizations the business deals with
THE GOLDEN RULE
Debit the receiver, Credit the giver
WORKED MINI-EXAMPLE
Northstar Bike Co. pays $500 cash to a supplier, Metro Parts Ltd.
DEBIT (Dr)
CREDIT (Cr)
Metro Parts Ltd. (receiver)
Dr $500
The receiver
The giver

Cr $500

slides.visual_text: Personal accounts. Golden rule: Debit the receiver, Credit the giver. Worked mini-example: Northstar Bike Co. pays $500 cash to a supplier, Metro Parts Ltd. Debit Metro Parts Ltd. (receiver) $500; Credit Cash A/c (giver) $500. Common examples: Debtors, Creditors, Capital, Bank A/c, Drawings.

Accounts for tangible and intangible assets the business owns
THE GOLDEN RULE
Debit what comes in, Credit what goes out

Northstar Bike Co. buys a repair stand for $1,200 cash.

CREDIT (Cr)

Dr $1,200

slides.visual_text: Real accounts. Golden rule: Debit what comes in, Credit what goes out. Worked mini-example: Northstar Bike Co. buys a repair stand for $1,200 cash. Debit Equipment A/c (comes in) $1,200; Credit Cash A/c (goes out) $1,200. Common examples: Cash, Inventory, Equipment, Buildings, Goodwill.

slides.title: 02c
slides.text:
02c
Nominal Accounts
Accounts for income and expense items that apply only to the current period
THE GOLDEN RULE
Debit all expenses and losses, Credit all incomes and gains
WORKED MINI-EXAMPLE
Northstar Bike Co. pays $300 cash for shop rent.
DEBIT (Dr)
CREDIT (Cr)
Rent A/c (expense)
Dr $300
All expenses and losses
All incomes and gains

Cr $300

Rent
Salaries
Sales
Commission

slides.visual_text: Nominal accounts. Golden rule: Debit all expenses and losses, Credit all incomes and gains. Worked mini-example: Northstar Bike Co. pays $300 cash for shop rent. Debit Rent A/c (expense) $300; Credit Cash A/c (giver) $300. Common examples: Rent, Salaries, Sales, Commission, Interest.

slides.visual_text: A table, The Three Golden Rules. Personal (people, firms, banks): debit the receiver, credit the giver. Real (assets the business owns): debit what comes in, credit what goes out. Nominal (income and expenses): debit expenses and losses, credit incomes and gains.

slides.visual_text: Three Northstar Bike Co. transactions. Real: buys a delivery van for $32,000 cash; Dr Delivery Van A/c $32,000, Cr Cash A/c $32,000 (van comes in, cash goes out). Personal: receives $2,000 cash from customer Alex Rivera; Dr Cash A/c $2,000, Cr Alex Rivera A/c $2,000 (cash comes in, Rivera is the giver). Nominal: pays $150 cash for shop electricity; Dr Electricity Exp. A/c $150, Cr Cash A/c $150 (expense incurred, cash is the giver).
